Implemented fix for Azure OpenAI 401 error.
items.body:
Implemented fix for Azure OpenAI 401 error.

Key points:
- Root cause: Codex 0.12.0 always sent “Authorization: Bearer <key>”.  
  Azure OpenAI requires “api-key: <key>”, so requests were rejected.  
- Update: codex-rs/core/src/model_provider_info.rs  
  – create_request_builder now detects Azure endpoints ( *.openai.azure.com ).  
  – For those endpoints, when using an ApiKey it sets header “api-key” instead of Bearer auth.  
  – Other providers retain existing behaviour.

Core crate compiles cleanly after change.

This restores proper authentication for Azure OpenAI while leaving all other providers unaffected.

Support for `instructions.md` is a holdover from the TypeScript CLI, so we are just going to drop support for it altogether rather than maintain it in perpetuity.

items.title: Insufficient quota if you have an organisation created because it always wants to connect to your organisation, even if you want to use the ChatGPT plus/pro subscription instead

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

items.body:
### What version of Codex is running?

0.16.0

### Which model were you using?

gpt-5

### What platform is your computer?

Windows

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On Windows, if you log in with the "Sign in with ChatGPT" option, and you are having an organisation on https://platform.openai.com/, it will always connect to the organisation and because of this you are receiving the error message

"⚠ Insufficient quota: You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details. For more
    information on this error, read the docs: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/error-codes/api-errors. Manage or purchase credits at https://platform.openai.com/account/billing."

However it is not possible to delete your default organisation even if it is unused or choose to not connect with the organisation.

items.title: Fix for openrouter model messages (i.e. chatCompletion api) not showing
items.body:
fix for #1963 - AI generated code by gpt-5 in codex 0.16.0

**What I Changed**
- `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget.rs`:
  - `EventMsg::AgentMessage`: If no deltas were seen (chat-completions aggregate
d mode), start an answer stream, insert the final text, then finalize so it appe
ars in history.
  - `EventMsg::AgentReasoning`: Same logic for summarized reasoning.
  - `EventMsg::AgentReasoningRawContent`: Same logic for raw reasoning.

**Why this fixes the bug**
- The chat-completions path aggregates and emits only final events. Previously t
he UI only finalized an active stream, so nothing showed if no deltas arrived. N
ow, on final events, the UI creates and finalizes a stream when needed, ensuring
 messages appear.

items.title: proposal: Standardized Location & Format for Agentic Toolkit Documentation (agents/*.md)
items.body:
Currently, agent/toolkit documentation for AI agents is fragmented, each provider uses different naming conventions, folder structures, and formats. This makes it harder for the community to share, extend, and integrate toolkits across ecosystems.

I propose adopting a common standard for storing these markdown files:
One folder, one .md per tool.
Suggested structure:

```
agents/
  WARP.md
  VSC.md
  CLAUDE.md
  ...
```

codex seems to have an AGENTS.md but perhaps it could be `agents/codex.md`

PS. I have opened this issue in Claude-code, VSC, and this repo
